key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves multiscale CFD surrogate forecasting by combining spectral encoding, PDE-aware attention, and self-supervised physics pretraining to better recover localized flow structures.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical surrogate modeling route for accelerating real-world CFD and fluid-structure interaction simulations while preserving accuracy on both global and local flow features.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding for multiscale flow representation
Physics-biased self-attention guided by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining with Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Evaluated on cylinder-wake and fluid-structure-interaction benchmarks, the model achieved best overall performance, including 0.05875 all-channel NMSE and 0.97019 PCC on cylinder wake, and 2.70×10^-4 all-channel NMSE on FSI versus 4.02×10^-4 for the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Performance is reported under a shared local benchmark protocol, so generalization to higher Reynolds numbers, different geometries, or longer rollout horizons still needs validation.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
